name: Paper plugin
summary: A server plugin for Paper 26.x: Gradle, plugin.yml and a JavaPlugin class.
description: A Gradle (Kotlin DSL) project that builds a plugin jar for a Paper server: plugin.yml, a main class that extends JavaPlugin and, as options, a command and an event listener. Players need nothing installed. Needs JDK 25, which Gradle can download by itself.

options.label: Plugin name
options.patternHelp: start with a letter, at least two characters; letters, digits, spaces, - and _ only
options.help: The name in plugin.yml is this without spaces (My Plugin becomes MyPlugin).

options.label: Author
options.patternHelp: start with a letter; letters, digits, spaces, - and _ only
options.help: Goes into the Java package (com.author.pluginname) and plugin.yml.

options.label: Paper version
options.help: The Minecraft version of the server. Sets the paper-api dependency and api-version. Only 26.1 and newer: older versions name the dependency differently.

options.label: Gradle version
options.help: The Gradle that the wrapper downloads. Java 25 needs Gradle 9.1 or newer.

options.label: Example command
options.help: A slash command named after the plugin.

options.label: Example event listener
options.help: A class that greets players when they join.

next: Open the folder in IntelliJ IDEA and let it import the Gradle project. From a terminal instead, run once: gradle wrapper
Build the jar: gradlew build. It lands in build\libs.
Copy the jar into the plugins folder of a Paper server and restart the server (do not use /reload).
Look for the plugin's enabled line in the server console, or run /plugins.
Your code starts in onEnable in the main class.
